citations.title: Definitions (home care agency; home care services)
citations.requirement: Home care services include in-home aide services involving hands-on care. Companion, sitter, respite and homemaker alone are 'home assistance services' (G.S. 131E-136(1b)); they count as home care only when combined with other home care services.

citations.title: Licensure requirements
citations.requirement: No operating without a DHHS license. Nonrefundable annual fee is $510. License is issued only for the named premises and persons, is not transferable without written DHHS approval, and must be posted conspicuously on the premises.

citations.title: Deemed status for accredited agencies
citations.requirement: Commission rules deem an agency licensed without further review if it is accredited (e.g., Joint Commission, NLN, NC Accreditation Commission for In-Home Aide Services) for all services it provides.

citations.title: Rules and enforcement
citations.requirement: Rules must define in-home aide geographic service areas and staffing qualifications, bar hiring Health Care Personnel Registry listees, require owner training, and set advertising limits. DHSR inspects each agency at least every 3 years.

citations.title: Inspection; client record access; DHSR hotline notice
citations.requirement: Before releasing information or allowing record inspections, advise each client in writing of the right to object in writing. Give each client written notice of the DHSR hotline number before care or at the initial evaluation visit.

citations.title: Adverse action on a license
citations.requirement: DHHS may suspend, revoke, annul, withdraw, recall, cancel or amend a license for substantial failure to comply with Part 3 or its rules. Chapter 150B (APA) governs appeals.

citations.title: Unlicensed operation: penalties and injunction
citations.requirement: Knowingly operating without a license is a Class 3 misdemeanor (fine up to $500). DHHS must seek injunctions against unlicensed operation and may seek injunctive relief if a person hinders its duties.

citations.title: Smoking prohibited in client homes
citations.requirement: Agency must prohibit employees (including contractors) from smoking while providing services in a client's home and must tell clients of the prohibition. Administrative penalty up to $200 per violation.

citations.title: Declaration of home care clients' rights
citations.requirement: Fifteen client rights, including: plan-of-care participation; dignity and privacy; confidentiality; freedom from abuse, neglect and exploitation; grievances without reprisal; written statement of charges; refuse services; on-call and supervisor access; 10-day license-action notice.

citations.title: Notice to client
citations.requirement: At the initial evaluation visit or before services, give each client the rights declaration, client-responsibility policies, agency complaint contact, and DHSR section address and phone. Keep signed receipts in agency files.

citations.title: Implementation of client rights
citations.requirement: The home care agency director is responsible for implementing the Bill of Rights. Each agency must provide appropriate training to implement it.

citations.title: Enforcement and investigation; agency complaint duty
citations.requirement: Agency must investigate client or family complaints within 72 hours and document the complaint and its resolution. DHSR starts investigations immediately (life-threatening), within 24 hours (abuse), 48 hours (neglect), 2 weeks (other).

citations.title: Confidentiality of records and complainants
citations.requirement: DHHS may inspect client records at the agency to investigate alleged violations. DHHS must keep complainants and inspected records confidential.

citations.title: Waiver of rules during emergencies
citations.requirement: During a declared state of emergency or disaster, DHSR may temporarily waive Commission rules for home care agencies. Agencies should track and follow DHSR waiver notices.

citations.title: Criminal history check of applicants
citations.requirement: Submit the criminal history check request within 5 business days of a conditional offer of employment (per DHSR Home Care FAQ, rev. 5/30/25).

citations.title: Definitions
citations.requirement: Defines ADLs, IADLs (including medication reminders), extensive vs. limited assistance, hands-on care, in-home aide services, plan of care, and 'health care practitioner' (G.S. 90-640(a)). Policies must use these terms.

citations.title: License
citations.requirement: Each agency premises must obtain its own license unless exempt under G.S. 131E-136(3).

citations.title: Application, issuance, posting
citations.requirement: Applicants with no prior home care ownership must complete DHSR-approved training before a license is issued. One-year license. Post the license and a door sign with the agency name. License is non-transferable.

citations.title: Notices to DHSR: ownership/name, new service, discontinued service
citations.requirement: Written notice at least 30 days before an ownership or name change, and 30 days before adding a service category. Notify DHSR in writing if a licensed service is discontinued or unavailable for 6 continuous months.

citations.title: Inspections
citations.requirement: Inspections may occur at any time. Allow immediate access to premises and records or the survey is terminated. File a plan of correction within 10 working days. DHSR may visit clients' homes with client permission.

citations.title: Multiple premises
citations.requirement: For multi-site operators, DHSR may sample-inspect and, on 72 hours' notice, require records (including personnel records) at the inspected site. Sites may share staff and centralize records.

citations.title: Compliance with laws
citations.requirement: Comply with all federal, state and local law, including Social Security Act 1128B and 42 USC 1320a-7a and 7b (false statements, kickbacks). Staff must hold current NC licenses/registrations. Accredited agencies send DHSR survey reports within 30 days.

citations.title: Adverse action
citations.requirement: DHSR may reduce a license to provisional or revoke it, including for any failure that endangers client health, safety or welfare. A provisional license must be posted in place of the full license. Appeals follow G.S. 150B.

citations.title: Required written policies
citations.requirement: Governing body must adopt written policies on 11 topics: scope of services; admission and discharge; supervision; plan of care; emergency care in the home; record return timeframe; personnel qualifications; org chart; program evaluation; confidentiality; referrals.

citations.title: Agency director and supervisor
citations.requirement: Director must be a health care practitioner, or have 2 years' home care/G.S. 131E or 122C management experience, or hold a bachelor's degree plus 1 year. Designate a service supervisor, document duties, and notify DHSR in writing within 5 working days of a vacancy.

citations.title: Responsibility for services; geographic service area policy
citations.requirement: Agency keeps ultimate responsibility for contracted services. Written policy must name the geographic area for each service. Give DHSR 30 days' written notice before expanding the service area without a new site.

citations.title: Administrative, financial and statistical records
citations.requirement: Keep the annual home care budget available for inspection. Keep statistical records (staff FTEs, client demographics, units of service). Retain these records at least 3 years. Keep home care finances separately identifiable if part of a larger entity.

citations.title: Infection control, OSHA and TB screening
citations.requirement: Written infection control/communicable disease policies consistent with 15A NCAC 19A and 29 CFR 1910. Hands-on staff need a baseline TB skin test; positives need noninfectious status before assignment. Use Form DHHS 3405.

citations.title: Health Care Personnel Registry bar
citations.requirement: Do not hire, directly or by contract, anyone with a substantiated finding on the NC Health Care Personnel Registry (G.S. 131E-256(a)(1)).

citations.title: Personnel policies and job descriptions
citations.requirement: Written policies on personnel record content, orientation and in-service education; keep in-service attendance records. Written job descriptions for every position. Assign staff only to duties they are trained, competent and licensed for. No hour counts are set.

citations.title: Personnel record contents and retention
citations.requirement: Per employee: application, signed job description, references, TB records, Hep B vaccine or declination, annual bloodborne/airborne training, annual evaluation, credential checks, competency verification. Keep 1 year after termination.

citations.title: RN-verified core competencies for aides not on the Nurse Aide Registry
citations.requirement: For aides hired after 4/1/2009 not on the registry, an RN must verify six core skills: mobility/transfers, bath/shower, toileting, dressing, eating, continence care.

citations.title: Evaluation (annual program evaluation; 90-day record review)
citations.requirement: Governing body does an annual comprehensive evaluation (clients served, hours, outcomes, staff adequacy, non-acceptances, discharge reasons) and reviews a sample of active and closed client records every 90 days. Document evaluators, methods and actions.

citations.title: Client rights and responsibilities
citations.requirement: Give each client written notice of rights and responsibilities before care or at the initial evaluation visit. Document that clients were informed (G.S. 131E-144.3), give G.S. 131E-144.4 notices, and comply with G.S. 131E-144.6(b).

citations.title: Acceptance of clients for service
citations.requirement: Written intake policies: staff adequacy and absence coverage, home suitability, family availability, scope and area, referral-source notice when needs can't be met, 48 hours' notice before reducing or ending service (listed exceptions), referral to other agencies.

citations.title: In-home aide services: plan of care, Nurse Aide Registry, permitted duties
citations.requirement: Plan of care signed by practitioner and client, copy kept in home, with assistance level per ADL. Aides giving extensive assistance must be on the Nurse Aide Registry. Aides may assist with self-administration of ordered medications and must report changes.

citations.title: Initial in-home assessment and practitioner availability
citations.requirement: Health care practitioner assesses in the client's home before the plan of care (social, mental, physical, environmental, economic, ADLs, IADLs), signed and dated. Practitioner must be available for supervision and consultation.

citations.title: Block grant agencies; in-home aide geographic limit
citations.requirement: In-home aide service area is limited to the agency's county, contiguous counties, or within 90 minutes' driving time, whichever is greater. HCCBG/SSBG agencies must also follow 10A NCAC 06A and 06X.

citations.title: Caregiver competency and delegated supervision
citations.requirement: Assign caregivers only tasks they have demonstrated to the health care practitioner, with documentation kept. Supervision may be delegated by agency policy only if the practitioner stays available and accountable.

citations.title: Supervisory visits
citations.requirement: Practitioner makes a supervisory visit to each client's home every 90 days (caregiver present or not), and annually while the caregiver is providing care. Record date, findings, signature. Document corrective action. Practitioner available during service hours.

citations.title: Arrangements for services with other agencies or individuals
citations.requirement: Contracted services need a signed written agreement with 10 listed terms (services, term, fees, licensure verification, supervision, equal personnel standards, documentation, geographic area). Review annually.

citations.title: Plan of care policies
citations.requirement: Written policies must ensure services and items to be provided are specified under a plan of care.

citations.title: Case review and plan of care
citations.requirement: Plan of care is built with the client and reviewed every 90 days by the practitioner. It must state service type, frequency and duration, restrictions, safety measures and goals. Notify the physician of changes if physician orders are required.

citations.title: Orders (when required for in-home aide services)
citations.requirement: When orders for in-home aide services are required, a prescriber signs them and the original goes in the client record. Care may begin on a verbal order in the interim.

citations.title: Service records: requirement
citations.requirement: Written record policies. Client name on every page, true entry dates, 'late entry' labeling. Originals stay secure on premises. Removed records return within 5 working days with a sign-out log. Retain 5 years after discharge (minors: until 3 years after age 18).

citations.title: Content of record
citations.requirement: Admission data (ID, signed rights form, next of kin, referral source, home assessment) and service data (initial assessment, goals, client approval, dated and signed service entries, discharge summary, coordination evidence).

citations.title: Companion/sitter/respite agency director
citations.requirement: Only for non-hands-on (companion, sitter, respite) services: director needs a high school diploma or GED plus health care practitioner status or 1 year of experience. Does not replace .1001 for in-home aide services.

citations.title: Supervision of companion, sitter and respite staff
citations.requirement: For non-hands-on staff: contact the client every 3 months and visit the home at least every 6 months, plus annually while the aide is in the home. Document each visit. Supervisor is available on-site when necessary.

citations.title: OSHA General Industry Standards
citations.requirement: 13J incorporates 29 CFR 1910 by reference. Infection control policies must comply with it, and hands-on staff need annual airborne and bloodborne pathogen training under the agency exposure control plan.

citations.title: State Plan Personal Care Services in In-Home Settings (amended Jan. 1, 2026)
citations.requirement: In-home PCS requires a service authorization for a set number of hours and an approved provider service plan. Do not schedule beyond authorized hours (per fact-checked research).

citations.title: NC CAP/DA waiver (Nov. 1, 2024 - Oct. 31, 2029)
citations.requirement: CAP/DA is the governing waiver for in-home aide services to adults at risk of institutionalization. Referrals and assessments run through NCLIFTSS (833-522-5429) (per fact-checked research).

citations.title: Electronic visit verification for PCS and home health
citations.requirement: EVV is required for Medicaid PCS and CAP/DA visits. NC Medicaid expects at least 85% of visit data captured electronically (manual entries 15% or less). Sandata is the state vendor for NC Medicaid Direct (per fact-checked research).

citations.title: HIPAA Privacy Rule: administrative requirements
citations.requirement: Covered entities, including agencies that bill Medicaid electronically, need privacy policies, a privacy official, workforce training, safeguards and a complaint process. Not fetched; confirm in Step 2.

citations.title: FLSA: application to domestic service (home care)
citations.requirement: Third-party home care employers cannot use the companionship or live-in overtime exemptions, so hours over 40 per week are paid at 1.5x. Not fetched; confirm in Step 2.

citations.title: HCBS waiver settings requirements
citations.requirement: CAP/DA services must meet federal HCBS setting and person-centered planning requirements. Not fetched; confirm in Step 2.

policies.title: Agency Organization Chart and Governing Body Structure
state_specifics: The governing body adopts the written policies required by 10A NCAC 13J .1001(a), including the organizational chart.
The chart shows governing body, agency director, service supervisor/RN, scheduler/intake and caregivers.
The director is responsible for implementing the client Bill of Rights (G.S. 131E-144.5).
Update the chart whenever the director or supervisor changes.

policies.title: Licensure, License Posting, Notices to DHSR, Inspections and Plan of Correction
state_specifics: A DHHS license is required to operate. It covers only the named premises and persons, is non-transferable without written DHHS approval, and expires Dec. 31 (annual fee $510, nonrefundable).
Post the license conspicuously on the premises and post a door sign with the agency name. A provisional license is posted in place of the full license.
Give DHSR written notice 30 days before an ownership or name change or before adding a service category. Notify DHSR if a licensed service is unavailable for 6 continuous months.
Inspections are unannounced. Give immediate access to premises and records or the survey is terminated. File a plan of correction within 10 working days.
DHSR section phone 919-855-4620; DHSR.homecare@dhhs.nc.gov.

policies.title: Scope of Services
state_specifics: List the licensed service categories (in-home aide services; companion/sitter/respite only if licensed).
Use the .0901 terms: ADL, IADL, limited vs. extensive assistance, hands-on care.
State the services the agency does not provide, such as skilled nursing and medication administration.
Advertising must not claim services the agency is not licensed to provide.

policies.title: Emergency Care in the Home and Emergency Preparedness
state_specifics: Caregiver steps for a medical emergency: call 911, stay with the client, notify the supervisor/RN, notify the family or representative, and document.
An RN is on call for consultation during all aide hours.
The agency maintains a client-level disaster plan and a continuity plan for staff absence.
During a declared emergency, follow any DHSR rule-waiver notices (G.S. 131E-112).

policies.title: Geographic Service Area
state_specifics: The policy names the geographic area for each licensed service.
In-home aide service area is the agency county, contiguous counties, or within 90 minutes' driving time, whichever is greater.
Screen each intake address against the area before acceptance.
Give DHSR 30 days' written notice before expanding the service area without a new site.

policies.title: Agency Director: Qualifications, Job Description and Vacancy Notice
state_specifics: The director is a health care practitioner, or has 2 years of home care or G.S. 131E/122C management experience, or holds a bachelor's degree plus 1 year of experience.
Keep a written job description and documented qualification proof.
Notify DHSR in writing within 5 working days of a director vacancy.
Name a qualified backup director in advance.

policies.title: Director Standard for Companion/Sitter/Respite-Only Services (If Applicable)
state_specifics: Applies only to non-hands-on companion, sitter and respite services.
The director needs a high school diploma or GED plus health care practitioner status or 1 year of experience.
It does not replace .1001 for in-home aide services.
If the agency is licensed only for in-home aide services, state this and keep the policy as a reference.

policies.title: Service Supervisor Designation and Job Description
state_specifics: Designate a service supervisor and document the duties.
The RN/health care practitioner must be available for supervision and consultation during all service hours.
An LPN may not perform assessments or supervisory visits for in-home aide services (DHSR FAQ).
Notify DHSR within 5 working days if the supervisor position is vacant.

policies.title: Job Descriptions for All Positions
state_specifics: A written job description is required for every position, with qualifications and specific responsibilities.
Staff are assigned only duties they are trained, competent and licensed for.
The employee signs the job description, which is kept in the personnel file.
Cover director, RN/supervisor, scheduler/intake, in-home aide and any other positions.

policies.title: Annual Program Evaluation and Quality Improvement
state_specifics: The governing body completes the evaluation annually.
Review clients served, hours, outcomes, staff adequacy, non-acceptances and discharge reasons.
Document the evaluators, methods and actions taken.
Use the findings for performance improvement.

policies.title: Client Record Review Every 90 Days
state_specifics: Review a sample of active and closed client records every 90 days.
Document the reviewers, method and corrective actions.
Check plan-of-care reviews, supervisory visits and signed rights notices.
Report results to the governing body.

policies.title: Infection Control and Communicable Disease Exposure
state_specifics: Policies must be consistent with 15A NCAC 19A and incorporate 29 CFR 1910.
Identify employee risk categories by job (hands-on aides, RN/supervisor, office-only staff).
Cover hand hygiene, PPE, sharps, waste, client illness and exclusion of ill staff.
Review the policy annually.

policies.title: Bloodborne Pathogen Policy and Training
state_specifics: All hands-on in-home caregivers need annual bloodborne and airborne pathogen training.
Training records go in the personnel file.
Training follows the agency exposure control plan.
Update training when procedures or tasks change.

policies.title: Tuberculosis (TB) Screening
state_specifics: Hands-on staff need a baseline TB skin test before client assignment.
A positive result requires documented noninfectious status before assignment.
Use Form DHHS 3405 per .1003(b).
TB records are kept in the personnel file.

policies.title: Hepatitis B Immunization or Declination
state_specifics: Offer the Hepatitis B vaccine to at-risk staff at no cost.
Keep a vaccine record or a signed declination in each personnel file.
The employee may accept the vaccine later.

policies.title: Exposure Control Plan and Post-Exposure Follow-Up
state_specifics: The written exposure control plan lists job categories at risk and the controls used.
Post-exposure steps: immediate first aid, report to the supervisor, medical evaluation and confidential follow-up.
Document each exposure incident.
Review the plan annually.

policies.title: Employee and Client Confidentiality (HIPAA)
state_specifics: Before releasing information or allowing record inspection, advise each client in writing of the right to object in writing (G.S. 131E-141).
Designate a privacy official and train all staff.
Cover caregiver texting, social media and records kept in the home.
Cover employee personnel and health information.

policies.title: Policy Review and Document Control
state_specifics: The governing body approves the policies in .1001(a) and reviews them at least annually.
Keep a version log with dates and approvals.
Keep the manual available to staff.
Make the manual immediately available to DHSR surveyors.

policies.title: Compliance, Fraud Prevention, Billing Integrity and Administrative Records
state_specifics: Comply with all federal, state and local law, including the false-statement and kickback laws named in .0906.
Keep the annual home care budget and statistical records (FTEs, client demographics, units of service) at least 3 years.
Keep home care finances separately identifiable if the agency is part of a larger entity.
If accredited, send DHSR survey reports within 30 days.
Staff must hold current NC licenses or registrations.

policies.title: Client Rights and Responsibilities
state_specifics: Give the 15-right declaration (G.S. 131E-144.3) and client responsibilities before care or at the initial evaluation visit.
Keep a signed receipt in the client record.
Also give the agency complaint contact and the DHSR section address and phone (G.S. 131E-144.4).
Train all staff on implementing the Bill of Rights.

policies.title: Client Complaints and Grievances (with DHSR Hotline)
state_specifics: Investigate client or family complaints within 72 hours and document the complaint and its resolution.
Give each client written notice of the DHSR hotline number before care or at the initial evaluation visit. Insert the current number from DHSR before printing (1-800-624-3004; confirm).
No reprisal for complaints.
DHSR section phone 919-855-4620.

policies.title: Coordination of and Referral To and From Community Agencies
state_specifics: When needs cannot be met, notify the referral source and refer the client to other agencies.
Document each referral and coordination contact in the client record.
Keep a current community resource list (DSS, Area Agency on Aging, NCLIFTSS, hospitals, hospice).

policies.title: Acceptance of Clients for Service
state_specifics: Written intake criteria: staff adequacy and absence coverage, home suitability, family availability, and scope and area of service.
Notify the referral source when needs cannot be met.
Give 48 hours' notice before reducing or ending service, subject to the listed exceptions.
Refer to other agencies when appropriate.

policies.title: Initial In-Home Assessment (In-Home Aide Services)
state_specifics: A health care practitioner (RN) assesses in the client's home before the plan of care.
Assess social, mental, physical, environmental and economic status, ADLs and IADLs.
Sign and date the assessment.
The practitioner is available for supervision and consultation.

policies.title: Plan of Care Development, Orders and 90-Day Review
state_specifics: The plan of care is built with the client and signed by the practitioner and client. Keep a copy in the home.
State assistance level per ADL, service type, frequency, duration, restrictions, safety measures and goals.
The practitioner reviews it every 90 days.
When orders are required, a prescriber signs them and the original goes in the record. Care may begin on a verbal order in the interim.
Notify the physician of changes when physician orders are required.

policies.title: No Smoking in Client Homes
state_specifics: Employees and contractors may not smoke while providing services in a client's home.
Tell each client of the prohibition at intake.
Administrative penalty up to $200 per violation.
Staff sign an acknowledgment at orientation.

policies.title: Supervision of Staff and Supervisory Visits
state_specifics: The practitioner makes a supervisory visit to each client's home every 90 days, with or without the caregiver present.
The practitioner also visits annually while the caregiver is providing care.
Record the date, findings and signature, and document corrective action.
Delegated supervision is allowed only if the practitioner stays available and accountable.
Companion/sitter staff: contact the client every 3 months and visit the home at least every 6 months (.1504).

policies.title: Arrangements for Services with Other Agencies or Individuals
state_specifics: Use a signed written agreement with the 10 required terms.
Verify the contractor's licensure and apply equal personnel standards.
The agency keeps ultimate responsibility for contracted services.
Review each agreement annually.

policies.title: Admission, Discharge, Transfer and Discontinuation of Services
state_specifics: Give 48 hours' notice before reducing or ending service, subject to the listed exceptions.
Complete a discharge summary in the client record.
Refer to other providers and document coordination.
Discharge reasons feed the annual program evaluation.

policies.title: Health Care Personnel Registry (HCPR) Reporting
state_specifics: Applies to allegations against health care personnel, such as abuse, neglect, exploitation or misappropriation of client property. The policy follows 10A NCAC 13O .0102, as listed on the DHSR checklist; confirm the rule text and time frame before publication.
The agency must not hire anyone with a substantiated HCPR finding.
HCPR phone 919-855-3968.
Document each report and the investigation.

policies.title: Client Record Content, Handling and Retention
state_specifics: Client name on every page, true entry dates, and late entries labeled as such.
Originals stay secure on premises. Removed records return within 5 working days, with a sign-out log.
Service records are completed and returned to the agency within the stated time frame.
Retain 5 years after discharge (minors: until 3 years after age 18).
Record content: admission data (ID, signed rights form, next of kin, referral source, home assessment) and service data (assessment, goals, client approval, signed entries, discharge summary).

policies.title: Caregiver Permitted Duties and Medication Assistance
state_specifics: Assign only tasks listed in the plan of care and demonstrated by the caregiver.
Aides may assist with self-administration of ordered medications but may not administer them.
Medication reminders are an IADL.
Aides must report changes in condition to the supervisor.
Extensive-assistance tasks require a Nurse Aide Registry listing.

policies.title: Abuse, Neglect and Exploitation Prevention and Reporting
state_specifics: Clients have the right to be free from abuse, neglect and exploitation.
Suspected abuse, neglect or exploitation of a disabled or older adult is reported to the county DSS Adult Protective Services. Cite the state statute and confirm the time frame before publication.
Report to the HCPR (see CLN-11) and to the director immediately.
DHSR investigates abuse allegations within 24 hours and neglect within 48 hours.
Remove the accused caregiver from the client pending investigation.

policies.title: Incident Reporting and Documentation
state_specifics: Document all injuries, falls, property damage and complaints on an incident form.
The supervisor reviews each incident within the same business day.
Trend results in the annual program evaluation.
Keep incident reports available for DHSR review.

policies.title: Client Property, Gifts and Financial Exploitation Prevention
state_specifics: Staff may not accept gifts, loans or bequests, or use client funds or property for personal benefit.
Any shopping or cash handling needs a receipt log.
Report misappropriation to the HCPR and the county DSS (see CLN-11 and CLN-14).

policies.title: Nondiscrimination and Language Access
federal: Title VI of the Civil Rights Act
state_specifics: Provide interpreters and translated documents at no cost to clients.
No discrimination in acceptance or service on any protected basis.
Accommodate disabilities.

policies.title: Service Agreement, Rates and Billing Disclosure
state_specifics: Clients have the right to a written statement of charges (G.S. 131E-144.3).
Disclose rates, minimum hours, cancellation terms and payment methods.
Disclose the no-smoking rule and the DHSR notice at signing.
Have an attorney review the private-pay agreement.

policies.title: Scheduling, Missed Visits and Continuity of Care
state_specifics: The intake policy must address coverage for staff absence.
Notify the client and supervisor of a missed visit and arrange a replacement.
Log each missed visit and the reason.
The client has on-call and supervisor access (G.S. 131E-144.3).

policies.title: Change in Client Condition
state_specifics: Aides report changes in condition to the RN immediately.
The RN reassesses and updates the plan of care.
Notify the physician when physician orders are required.
Notify the family or representative per the client's wishes.

policies.title: Transporting Clients
state_specifics: Transport only if the plan of care authorizes it.
Require a valid license, registration, insurance and seat belts.
Document trip purpose, mileage and any incident.

policies.title: Caregiver Safety in the Home and Workplace Violence
state_specifics: Complete a home safety assessment at intake (G.S. 131E and .1101 home suitability).
Staff may leave an unsafe situation and must report it.
Report workplace violence incidents to the supervisor immediately and document them.

policies.title: Personnel Qualifications, Nurse Aide Registry and Credential Verification
state_specifics: State the qualifications for director, RN/supervisor, scheduler and aides.
Aides giving extensive assistance must be on the Nurse Aide Registry.
For aides hired after 4/1/2009 who are not on the registry, an RN verifies 6 core skills: mobility/transfers, bath/shower, toileting, dressing, eating and continence care.
Verify licenses and registrations at hire and annually.

policies.title: Competency Verification and Skills Validation
state_specifics: Assign caregivers only tasks they have demonstrated to the practitioner, with documentation kept.
Use a skills checklist signed by the RN.
Reassess competency periodically and after any change in task.

policies.title: Personnel Records Content and Retention
state_specifics: Contents: application, signed job description, references, TB record, Hepatitis B vaccine or declination, annual bloodborne/airborne training, annual evaluation, credential checks and competency verification.
Keep records 1 year after termination.
Records must be available at the licensed site for DHSR.

policies.title: Annual Performance Evaluation
state_specifics: Complete an evaluation for each employee annually and file it in the personnel record.
Review it with the employee and obtain a signature.

policies.title: In-Service Education
state_specifics: The rule sets no hour count. The agency sets annual in-service hours in this policy and follows them.
Keep attendance records.
Annual bloodborne and airborne pathogen training is required for hands-on staff.

policies.title: Orientation
state_specifics: Orientation topics: client rights and Bill of Rights training, confidentiality, abuse reporting, infection control, emergencies, the no-smoking rule and the plan of care.
Complete orientation before any client assignment.
Document the date and content.

policies.title: Criminal Background Investigation and HCPR Check
state_specifics: Submit the criminal history check request within 5 business days of a conditional offer.
Do not hire, directly or by contract, anyone with a substantiated HCPR finding (.1003(c)).
Keep results in the personnel file.
HCPR phone 919-855-3968.

policies.title: Wage, Hour and Overtime Compliance
state_specifics: Third-party home care employers cannot use the companionship or live-in exemptions, so hours over 40 per week are paid at 1.5x.
Count travel time between clients and other compensable time.
NC minimum wage is $7.25 per hour.

policies.title: Staff Conduct and Professional Boundaries
state_specifics: Cover no gifts, no personal use of client property and no social media posts about clients.
Cover no smoking in the home (G.S. 131E-143).
Violations lead to discipline and may require a report to the HCPR.

policies.title: Personnel Record Review Checklist for Surveyors
state_specifics: Audit each file for: application, signed job description, references, TB record, Hepatitis B vaccine or declination, annual training, annual evaluation, credential checks and competency verification.
Verify the criminal history request date was within 5 business days of the conditional offer, and the HCPR check.
Verify Nurse Aide Registry listing or RN-verified core skills.

policies.title: Medicaid State Plan PCS (Clinical Coverage Policy 3L): Authorization and Service Plan
state_specifics: Services require a service authorization for a set number of hours and an approved provider service plan.
Do not schedule beyond authorized hours, and track authorization dates for each client.
PCS rate: $7.03 per unit (99509 HA/HB) effective Aug. 1, 2026. Confirm the unit length on the NC Medicaid fee schedule.

policies.title: CAP/DA Waiver Coordination and HCBS Settings Requirements
state_specifics: CAP/DA waiver 0132.R08.00 runs Nov. 1, 2024 to Oct. 31, 2029.
Referrals and assessments run through NCLIFTSS (833-522-5429).
Follow person-centered planning and HCBS setting requirements.
Do not depend on CAP/DA alone for census.

policies.title: Electronic Visit Verification and Timekeeping
state_specifics: EVV is required for Medicaid PCS and CAP/DA visits.
At least 85% of visit data must be captured electronically (manual entries 15% or less).
Sandata is the state vendor for NC Medicaid Direct. Plan-contracted providers use the plan's EVV solution.
Run weekly exception reports and reconcile EVV, authorizations and claims.

documents.title: Home Care Initial Survey Checklist
documents.form_number: No form number. The footer reads 'Rev 9/21 gdh'.
documents.issuer: NC DHHS Division of Health Service Regulation, Acute and Home Care Licensure and Certification Section
documents.version: Rev 9/21 gdh. This is the file currently linked from the DHSR 'Requirements for Establishing a Home Care Agency' page.
documents.how_used: This is the primary document. DHSR tells applicants to use it as their guide. After DHSR receives the application and fee, it emails the applicant to request the policies, procedures and personnel documents. The initial survey then reviews them for compliance. Items below are listed as the checklist words them, with the rule cites printed on the form.

documents.title: 10A NCAC 13J .1001, .1003, .1004 (Licensing of Home Care Agencies, Subchapter 13J rules)
documents.issuer: NC Medical Care Commission, published by the NC Office of Administrative Hearings; enforced by DHSR
documents.version: Current codified text of Subchapter 13J. The .1001 history note shows it was found necessary without substantive public interest, eff. June 25, 2016. The .1004 history note shows it readopted eff. June 1, 2018.
documents.how_used: This is the regulation text behind the checklist's cites. Rule .1001(a) lists the written policies the governing body must establish. Items from this document are marked 'doc 1' below. I could not retrieve the text of rules .1007, .1101, .1107, .1110, .1111, .1202, .1401, .1402, .1503 or .1504 in full, so the sub-requirements of those rules are not listed beyond what the checklist itself states.

official.notes: DHSR has no separate policy-manual form. The Home Care Initial Survey Checklist (Rev 9/21) is the review tool. Submission process: (1) The applicant mails the license application (hcapp.pdf), the fee, and proof of prior home care ownership or of DHSR-approved home care training to DHSR, 2712 Mail Service Center, Raleigh, NC 27699-2712. (2) DHSR emails to confirm receipt, then emails a request for the policies, procedures and personnel documents. (3) The initial survey is a desk review of those documents against the licensure rules. If no further information is needed, DHSR emails an approval letter with instructions for printing the license from the Enterprise system. Organize the manual in the checklist's order and group it under its three policy headings: Administrative Policies, Client Care Policies and Personnel Policies. Label each policy with the rule cite printed on the checklist so the surveyor can check each line. The checklist does not number its items, so item_id values above are built from the section name and rule cite. Cites are as printed on the checklist, including its '.1001 (5)' for emergency preparedness (the rule text places it at .1001(a)(5)). Three checklist lines also cover the Supporting Documentation section. Only the Agency Organization Chart is policy content and appears in the items above. The other Supporting Documentation lines are excluded as non-policy paperwork: proof of prior ownership, the training certificate, the premises lease, articles of incorporation, and the annual projected budget. The checklist has no cite for the bloodborne pathogen and Hepatitis B policy lines. Rule .1003(f)(5)-(6) covers Hepatitis B and pathogen training records. The checklist marks some items 'if applicable' (Companion Sitter Agency Director) or ties them to a service type (companion/sitter rules .1503-.1504). For a Personal Home Care (in-home aide) agency, the in-home aide cites (.1107, .1110) apply. The Personnel Record Review grid is a record check, not policy content. It covers the application, resume, signed job description, license verification, NA registry and Health Care Personnel Registry check, competency verification, TB proof, bloodborne pathogen training proof, Hepatitis B proof, orientation, reference checks, and signed criminal background consent. The checklist page was last modified in 2018, but the checklist PDF itself is Rev 9/21. Confirm with DHSR (919-855-4620, DHSR.homecare@dhhs.nc.gov) that no newer revision exists before submitting.
